review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions of `interpolation` and `endpointCoupling` in ComparatorChallenges/WeakHessian.lean. I also read Mathlib's `Measure.map_smul`, `ae_map_iff` and `ae_of_ae_map`. The proposed replacements have not been compiled. The details of the `rw` and `change` steps, and the unification of the let-bound `ξ`, are untested. I considered replacing `hp` with Mathlib's `isProbabilityMeasureSMul`, which needs a `NeZero θ` instance. I dropped it because the gain is small. The `rnDeriv_le_of_le_smul` calc and the final `simpa` looked fine.

findings.excerpt:
change (q • π).map _ = _
    rw [Measure.map_smul _ (continuous_eval_const t).measurable.aemeasurable]
    change q • interpolation π t = _
findings.problem: `he` states the scaling rule `interpolation (c • ν) t = c • interpolation ν t` only for `θ'` and `q⁻¹`. The same `Measure.map_smul _ (continuous_eval_const t).measurable.aemeasurable` is then rebuilt three more times. These are in `hξend` (twice, lines 143 and 147) and in `hs'` (line 164). Each use needs `change` steps to unfold `interpolation` as `Measure.map`. The proofs of `hξend` and `hs'` are mostly this unfolding and refolding. That hides the idea: scaling commutes with taking marginals, so `q • θ' = θ` transfers the equality.
findings.proposed_change:
State the scaling rule once, for arbitrary scalar and measure:
`have hsmul (c : ℝ≥0∞) (ν : Measure (Curve X)) (t : Time) : interpolation (c • ν) t = c • interpolation ν t := Measure.map_smul _ (continuous_eval_const t).measurable.aemeasurable`.
Then `he` is just `hsmul _ _ t`. `hξend` becomes
`show interpolation (q • π) t = _; rw [hsmul, ht, ← hsmul, hcanc]`.
`hs'` becomes
`change interpolation (q • π) timeHalf Bᶜ = 0 at hs; rw [hsmul, Measure.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul] at hs; exact (mul_eq_zero.mp hs).resolve_left hq`.
Alternatively, make `hsmul` a top-level lemma `interpolation_smul`.
findings.benefit: The measurability side condition is proved once, and the three `change ... map ...` unfoldings disappear. `hξend` then reads as the mathematical argument: push the scalar through, use `ht`, pull it back, apply `hcanc`.

findings.excerpt:
apply ae_of_ae_map (f := fun γ : Curve X => γ timeZero) (p := fun x => dist x o ≤ R) (continuous_eval_const timeZero).measurable.aemeasurable
    change ∀ᵐ x ∂interpolation π timeZero, dist x o ≤ R
findings.problem: There are two nearly identical pairs of proofs that differ only in `timeZero` versus `timeOne`. `hb0`/`hb1` repeat the long `ae_map_iff` term with the same measurability proof of `{x | dist x o ≤ R}`. `hπ0`/`hπ1` use `apply ae_of_ae_map` with explicitly supplied `f` and `p`, then `change`, then `rw [he0]; exact hb0`. The explicit arguments and the `change` exist only to steer elaboration.
findings.proposed_change:
Prove the marginal/pointwise equivalence once for any time, using the equation `interpolation ν t = Measure.map (fun γ => γ t) ν`:
`have hball : MeasurableSet {x : X | dist x o ≤ R} := measurableSet_le (continuous_id.dist continuous_const).measurable measurable_const`
`have hmarg (ν : Measure (Curve X)) (t : Time) : (∀ᵐ x ∂interpolation ν t, dist x o ≤ R) ↔ ∀ᵐ γ ∂ν, dist (γ t) o ≤ R := ae_map_iff (continuous_eval_const t).measurable.aemeasurable hball`.
Then `hb0 := (hmarg θ' timeZero).2 (hb'.mono fun _ h => h.1)` and `hb1` likewise with `h.2`. Also `hπ0 := (hmarg π timeZero).1 (by rw [he0]; exact hb0)` and `hπ1` likewise with `timeOne`, `he1` and `hb1`.
findings.benefit: The measurability proof and the `ae_map_iff` plumbing are written once. The four facts become one-line applications of the same statement, `hlen` follows unchanged, and the explicit `(f := …) (p := …)` arguments go away.

have hmeas : Measurable (fun γ : Curve X => (γ timeZero,γ timeOne)) :=
        (continuous_eval_const timeZero).measurable.prodMk
          (continuous_eval_const timeOne).measurable
findings.problem: The measurability proof for the endpoint map `γ ↦ (γ timeZero, γ timeOne)` is written out in `endpointCoupling_couples` (line 60, `hm`). It is written again inside the local `hs` here. Both times the term is a copy-paste. `hs` is also a general statement about `endpointCoupling (q • η)` that is buried inside one bullet of a long proof.
findings.proposed_change: Add one small lemma, e.g. `lemma measurable_endpoints : Measurable (fun γ : Curve X => (γ timeZero, γ timeOne)) := (continuous_eval_const timeZero).measurable.prodMk (continuous_eval_const timeOne).measurable`. Use it as `measurable_endpoints` in `endpointCoupling_couples`, where `hm` is then not needed. Use `measurable_endpoints.aemeasurable` inside `hs`, which makes the `hmeas` block disappear. Optionally lift `hs` to a lemma `QuadraticTransportCost_endpointCoupling_smul`.
findings.benefit: The duplicated 3-line term is stated once, and `hs` reduces to a single `simp only [QuadraticTransportCost, endpointCoupling, Measure.map_smul _ measurable_endpoints.aemeasurable, lintegral_smul_measure, smul_eq_mul]`. The main proof then concentrates on the scaling argument.
